prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 华东区门店2024年1—5月销量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "门店" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 105px
  col 2: header "1月" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
  col 3: header "2月" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 4: header "3月" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "4月" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
  col 6: header "5月" · longest unbreakable word 39px · one-line width 39px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 392px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 391px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare monthly sales performance across six East China stores for January–May 2024, making store-level trends and month-to-month differences easy to scan.","reading":"Readers anchor on the store name in column 1, then scan horizontally across the five month columns to read a trend; they also compare vertically within a month. Equal month columns are important because those five columns share the same unit and role.","groups":["Columns 2–6 (1月–5月) form one measure group: same unit, same role, and should stay equal-width for direct comparison.","Column 1 (门店) is the row-identifier group and should remain visually distinct from the measures."],"keep_intact":["All four-digit sales values in columns 2–6 must stay on one line without breaking, wrapping, or truncation.","Month headers 1月–5月 and the header 门店 should remain intact.","Store names must remain complete; they may break only between Chinese characters, never lose characters."],"may_wrap":["Store names in column 1 can wrap to two lines; a three-line fallback is acceptable only if row height permits.","Month headers are too short to need wrapping; numeric cells should never wrap."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [91, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60] · table 392×435px · row heights [39, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [76, 63, 63, 63, 63, 63] · table 392×435px · row heights [39, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66, 66] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [66, 65, 65, 65, 65, 65] · table 392×593px · row heights [39, 92, 92, 92, 92, 92, 92] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
